worksheet.title: Follow the Arrows
worksheet.subtitle: Follow the steps to find Bit's box
worksheet.learning_goal: I can follow arrow steps in order to find where Bit lands.

parts.title: Follow the steps in order
parts.text: Each ➡ moves Bit one box to the right. Follow the arrows in order, one box at a time, to see where Bit lands. The star is on box 4.

parts.title: Two steps
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1 and follows ➡ ➡. Which box does Bit land on? Write the box number.

parts.title: Four steps
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1 and follows ➡ ➡ ➡ ➡. Which box does Bit land on? Write the box number.

parts.title: You try — land on the star
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 2 and follows ➡ ➡. Which box does Bit land on? Is it the star? Write the box number.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Following steps in order, one at a time, is how you run an algorithm. Computers follow their steps exactly the same way.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children execute a sequence of ➡ moves on a 1D board and report Bit's landing box. Carrying out step-by-step directions in order is executing an algorithm — and the count of steps determines the result.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children follow a sequence of directional instructions.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child writes the landing box number.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: floor boxes 1-5 with a star on box 4 to walk the steps.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: from box 1, walk ➡ ➡ ➡ aloud — box 2, box 3, box 4. Bit lands on the star.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — two steps from box 1 lands on box 3.
3. YOU TRY: children do four steps (Ex 2 → box 5), then start from box 2 (Ex 3 → box 4, the star).
4. Connect: 'Computers follow their steps in order, exactly — just like Bit.'

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: counting box 1 as the first move — the first ➡ moves Bit OFF box 1 to box 2.
Simplify: walk each step on the floor and stop to name the box.
Extend: ask how many steps from box 1 reach box 5 (4), or start from box 3.
Movement option: call out arrows and have children take one step each, freezing on the landing box.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child counts the ➡ steps from the start box and writes the correct landing box for each program.
